text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.
LONDON - The FTSE 100 ended a featureless abbreviated session on a firmer note, scoring its third consecutive closing high.
The FTSE 100 blue-chip index settled up 5.3 points at 4,092.5, just 7.5 points below a record intra-day high reached last Friday.
FRANKFURT - The German share market was closed for the Christmas holiday and reopens on Friday.
The DAX index ended floor trade down 8.88 points at 2,845.57 on Monday. The IBIS DAX index closed electronic trade up 8.55 points at 2,844.09 on Monday.
PARIS - French shares finished the last session before Christmas with a very small gain in moderate volume.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 2.11 points or 0.09 percent at 2,289.55.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended quiet Christmas Eve trading slightly easier ahead of a two-day holiday. The market focused on CS Holding and Elektrowatt after CS said on Monday it was selling its 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt's industrial side to Siemens.
The broad Swiss Performance Index closed down 2.48 points at 2,472.71.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks fell sharply on worries about Japan's economic prospects, with the key Nikkei index falling 2.69 percent to a fresh 12-month low.
The benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares slid 528.75 points or 2.69 percent to close at 19,161.71.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed a half-day session slightly up in active pre-holiday trade, with year-end demand for the market's leaders giving the index a small boost.
The Hang Seng Index rose 10.13 points to end at 13,341.61.
SYDNEY - Australian shares closed just firmer on light volume with most investors absent from a shortened session ahead of the Christmas break on Wednesday and Thursday.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 0.9 points firmer at 2,381.4.
JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended largely stable with industrials easing slightly as players squared positions. Gold shares were also softer on a steady bullion price.
The overall index was up 9.5 points to 6,562.1, boosted by gains in the mining financial index. The industrial index lost 10.9 to 7,783.5 and the gold index 5.6 to 1,488.8 points.
